title: Rex Fleet Academy: Physics of the Lattice
format: Prestige sequential-art educational science-fiction drama; topic-based Academy lectures told as practical stories.
premise: Young Fleet cadets learn the physical rules that make corridor travel possible and the failure modes that make post-Shattering navigation dangerous. Each lecture turns an apparently abstract physics question into a practical problem that pilots, navigators, technicians, and engineers must solve together.
storyEngine: An instructor poses a deceptively simple physical question; cadets commit to an intuitive answer; a live practicum, field case, or historical reconstruction exposes the limit of that answer; the cohort must operate safely under uncertainty; the lecture closes on a more precise model that opens the next question.
canonPrinciples: The Lattice is treated as physical geometry with measurable consequences, not magic or a generic hyperspace dimension.
A corridor is a low-tension geometric travel volume, not a fixed tunnel with physical walls.
Public corridors are centered on BHA beacon chains, but the verified safe cross-section is broader than the beacon line.
Green means verified low tension. Red means unsafe or unverified because sensing or verification has failed.
Beacons verify corridor state; they do not create the underlying corridor.
Navigators may ride the inverse-tension gradient inside a verified volume rather than rigidly following the beacon centerline.
A path longer in ordinary coordinates may be shorter or easier in Lattice geometry.
Later issues may deepen mechanism, but the ultimate trigger of the Sundering remains unresolved unless explicitly reopened.

recurringFrame.primaryLocation: Rex Fleet Academy lattice sciences wing in the Core Worlds, with practical work aboard Academy training craft and controlled field exercises.
recurringFrame.tone: Exact, curious, practical, and occasionally dry. Students learn by making operational choices, not by passively receiving exposition.

firstLectureArc: Tomas begins by treating the beacon centerline as the corridor and a straight intercept as the fastest solution. During a live practicum aboard Vector Three, a red forward beacon stops the class inside the last verified volume. A calibration drone reveals that the inverse-tension gradient has bowed inside the still-safe cross-section. The cadets recover it by taking a curved route that initially moves away from the target but reduces structural load and effective Lattice distance. The debrief separates beacon, corridor, path, and map.

academyCurriculum.planStatus: Issue 1 is the complete default course. The former eight-entry lecture plan has been converted to candidate technical modules, not future issues.
academyCurriculum.issueCountPolicy: Default to one issue. Add Issue 2 or 3 only if source-text pacing and dramatization cannot responsibly fit the course into one; do not exceed three.
academyCurriculum.sourceTextProgram: See academy_source_program.json. Technical-paper caption adaptation is a pacing experiment, initially testing roughly 6–9 short source lines per page alongside demonstrations and practical examples.

productionIssues.title: The Shortest Path
productionIssues.focus: Corridor geometry, beacon volume, inverse tension, and riding the inversion.

candidateModules.title: Coherence
candidateModules.focus: Why a route remains one stable geometric solution and what it means when correct instruments stop agreeing.

candidateModules.title: Tides
candidateModules.focus: Slow changes in the local Lattice field and navigation through moving geometry.

candidateModules.title: Echoes
candidateModules.focus: Signal persistence, trapped propagation, and the physical basis of Memory Wells.

candidateModules.title: Drift
candidateModules.focus: Evolving phase relationships, failed rendezvous, and the limits of ordinary position and timekeeping.

candidateModules.title: The Mirrorfold
candidateModules.focus: Multiple propagation paths, duplicated perception, and navigation when sight is not a reliable guide.

candidateModules.title: Fracture
candidateModules.focus: Matter coupling to strained geometry and Fracture Blooms as physical records of field state.

candidateModules.title: The Sundering
candidateModules.focus: Apply the course backward to the historical collapse; distinguish increasingly understood mechanism from unresolved trigger.

courseArchitecture.continuationRule: Candidate modules are not future issue assignments. If the reconciled technical paper needs more room, combine the strongest modules into at most two additional issues.
courseArchitecture.castScope: Dr. Sera Kade and this cohort belong to this course package; other Academy courses may use different casts.
courseArchitecture.imgScope: Use a dedicated Physics of the Lattice IMG/reference project when visual production begins.
